statement: When no observed or tested HRmax exists, estimate HRmax as 208 - 0.7 x age and flag it as an age-predicted, low-confidence value. No sex, fitness or BMI adjustment.
appliesTo: Healthy adults without a measured HRmax

statement: Do not use 220 - age anywhere in the engine; it underestimates HRmax in adults older than about 30.
Attach an uncertainty of about 10.8 bpm (SEE) to any age-predicted HRmax and mark zones derived from it as approximate. Equation error is worst for athletes with unusually high or low true maxima.
appliesTo: Any plan using a predicted HRmax

statement: Replace the predicted HRmax with an observed maximum as soon as one exists. Accept observed maxima only from chest-strap (not optical) data on efforts that were maximal; never cap an observed value to the equation. Specific effort-validity criteria are an engineering default, not evidence-derived.
appliesTo: All athletes; especially those far from the population mean

statement: If only an old measured HRmax is available, age-adjust it downward by about 0.7 bpm per year elapsed, and mark it low confidence. Inference from the longitudinal slope, not a tested protocol.
appliesTo: Athletes with an old HRmax measurement

statement: Zone anchors in order of preference: tested thresholds or CS; proxies (GPS CS, DFA a1 0.75 from fresh chest-strap data, RPE/talk test); then %HRmax. HRR (Karvonen) is an acceptable fallback only if resting HR is reliable, but is not shown to beat %HRmax and has no evidence-based cut-offs here. Record the source of every boundary.
value: threshold/CS > proxies (DFA a1, RPE, talk test) > %HRmax or %HRR
appliesTo: All plan generation and zone display

statement: Use a three-domain model: LT1/VT1 separates moderate from heavy, critical speed separates heavy from severe. Do not define these boundaries as fixed percentages of HRmax. Treat the upper boundary as CS-based; RCP/VT2 and lactate-steady-state values sit at different workloads and are expressed as ranges.

Show each zone boundary as a range and re-estimate from rolling recent data. Evidence-based widths: about +/-11 bpm for DFA-a1-derived VT1 HR and +/-10.8 bpm for HRmax predicted from age. No evidence supports a width for other sources; conservative default of a visible band of about 5 bpm or about 5% pace for tested thresholds (engineering default).

Estimate critical speed as the slope of the distance-time line through at least three best grade-adjusted efforts between 400 m and 5 km (400, 800 and 5000 m worked best). Report performance-prediction error of about 8%. The rolling window for best efforts (default 90 days) is an engineering default.
value: slope of distance-time, >=3 best efforts 400 m-5 km
appliesTo: Runners with logged GPS data (recreational data in the source study)

statement: Limit continuous threshold work to at or slightly below CS: steady VO2 was held 0.5 km/h below CS and VO2max was reached at 0.4 km/h above it. A 0.5 km/h margin is supported only for well-trained men and runs up to 30 min; widen the margin for recreational athletes or longer bouts. CS is about 1.2 km/h (about 8%) faster than MLSS in the same runners.
appliesTo: Well-trained runners; extrapolation to others is a conservative default

statement: Treat running above CS as time-limited by D'. Plan reps above CS so that work above CS in a rep never reaches the estimated tolerable time at that speed. A numeric limit (default: each rep at most half of the time to exhaustion) is an engineering default; D' reconstitution during recovery is not covered by the corpus.

Flag a planned or actual first-half marathon pace above about 94% of CS as a risk of a >25% second-half slowdown. Typical sustained fractions of CS are about 93% for 2.5 h and about 79% for 6 h finishers. Do not extrapolate to ultra distances.

If chest-strap RR data with artifact correction exist, offer HR at DFA a1 = 0.75 from a fresh, non-fatigued incremental or easy-to-moderate effort as an optional VT1 estimate with an error band of about +/-11 bpm. Reject RR windows with more than about 3% artifacts. Never compute DFA a1 from optical HR.

Do not update thresholds from DFA a1 recorded when fatigued or late in a long run (ramp-2 bias -12.3 bpm; DFA a1 0.71 to 0.32 after a 6 h simulated ultramarathon with unchanged HR). Do not prescribe sustained running at a DFA a1 = 0.5 speed (6 of 21 athletes could not finish 20 min). A DFA a1 decline during a constant-pace run may be logged as a candidate fatigue/durability signal only, with no automatic plan change.
value: fresh state only; 0.5 not for sustained prescription
appliesTo: Runners using DFA a1, especially long-run and ultra athletes

statement: With no HR or pace threshold data, use Borg 6-20 RPE about 10-11 and the equivocal talk-test stage for VT1, and RPE 13-15 and a negative talk test for the RCP/VT2 region. Do not use Feeling Scale for the upper boundary, and do not convert to a 0-10 scale without another source.
appliesTo: Athletes without threshold data; talk-test evidence is mostly non-runners
